claim: David Grusch, a former Air Force intelligence officer who served as the National Reconnaissance Office's representative to the Pentagon's UAP Task Force, testified under oath on July 26, 2023 before the House Oversight and Accountability Committee's Subcommittee on National Security, the Border, and Foreign Affairs, at a hearing titled "Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena: Implications on National Security, Public Safety, and Government Transparency" (Serial No. 118-53). In his opening statement he said: "I was informed in the course of my official duties of a multi-decade UAP crash retrieval and reverse engineering program to which I was denied access to those additional read-ons when I requested it." Asked by Rep. Nancy Mace whether the government has the bodies of pilots from craft he said had crashed, he answered: "As I have stated publicly already in my News Nation interview, biologics came with some of these recoveries. Yes." Asked whether they were human or nonhuman: "Nonhuman, and that was the assessment of people with direct knowledge on the program I talked to that are currently still on the program." He said he could not produce the underlying documentation in open session. Asked by Rep. Jared Moskowitz how such a program would be funded, he answered "misappropriation of funds and self-fund," said he had "specific knowledge of that," and identified contractor Independent Research and Development (IR&D) charges as a mechanism. Grusch testified that his account rests on interviews with more than 40 officials and did not claim firsthand observation of any craft or body. The Department of Defense has said it found no verifiable information substantiating the claims, and AARO's March 2024 historical review reported no empirical evidence for reverse-engineering programs; both are findings by the department whose conduct is at issue. As of this writing no document, material sample or firsthand witness has been produced on either side of the question.

notes: Backstage. Quotes pulled from the GPO transcript PDF itself (pdftotext), not from press summaries — the clip circulating on social media is verbatim accurate against the record, which is worth knowing. What the record establishes is that a cleared former officer said these things under oath to Congress; it does not establish that the underlying events occurred, and the claim text is written so a reader cannot mistake one for the other. Grusch's own testimony is explicitly secondhand ('the assessment of people with direct knowledge'). AARO's 2024 Historical Record Report Volume I is now carried as its own card (2024-aaro-historical-record-001) so the department's position stands in its own words rather than as a closing clause here. The claim previously ended on the DoD denial, which handed an interested party the last word — corrected: the denial is stated, its source is named, and the card closes on what neither side has produced. Group A on the testimony; the substance is Group B.
